blocks.text: Jeremiah 40 stands within the book’s account of Judah under Babylonian domination: after Jerusalem’s destruction, Gedaliah is appointed over those left in the land, and the narrative later moves toward flight to Egypt. In a practical outline of the book’s received form, chapters 34–45 form a narrative section that includes this aftermath. The book’s long compositional and textual history is debated, so this outline helps locate the chapter without resolving questions about how the book took its final shape.
